sm: The speaker argues that the radical core of modern evolutionary theory is its claim that life results from an undirected process, which Darwin saw as replacing design. He cites 38 Nobel laureates and a Cornell survey in which 90 percent of leading evolutionary biologists reject a guided purpose. C.S. Lewis accepted Darwinism only as a modest biological theorem, one that explains how species lose features like wings but not how new features arise, nor the origin of life or reason. Lewis's main challenge was the human mind, drawing on Arthur Balfour's book Theism and Humanism and developing it in Miracles. He argued that explaining reason through natural selection undermines confidence in reason itself, noting Darwin's own doubts about trusting a mind descended from lower animals. For Lewis, if evolution produced the mind, it must have been directed by intelligent design.
